stories.headline: An Se-young defends her Asian Games badminton title
stories.summary: An Se-young of South Korea won the women's singles badminton gold at the 2026 Asian Games. She beat Akane Yamaguchi of Japan 21–17, 21–9 in the final. She is the first woman to win two singles titles at the Games, and the first to defend the title.

stories.headline: Morocco gets its first woman prime minister
stories.summary: King Mohammed VI received Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri at the Royal Palace on 29 September 2026 and appointed her prime minister of Morocco. She is the first woman to hold the office. A lawyer by training, she has been mayor of Marrakesh, first from 2009 to 2015 and then since 2021.

stories.headline: Tokyo counts 34 rainy days in a row
stories.summary: The Japan Meteorological Agency recorded rainfall in Tokyo for 34 consecutive days. It is the longest streak since records began in 1886. The previous record, one day shorter, was set in 2019.

stories.headline: Galápagos green turtles stayed close to home
stories.summary: Researchers tagged nine adult green sea turtles in the Galápagos in 2015 and followed them by satellite. None of them left the Galápagos Marine Reserve over the three years of the study, although the team had expected them to migrate to distant beaches in the western Pacific. Most stayed in shallow water close to the islands.

sources.excerpt: In badminton, South Korea's An Se-young wins the women's singles gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games, becoming the first woman to win two singles titles and the first to defend the title, defeating Japan's Akane Yamaguchi 21–17, 21–9.
An Se-young (born 5 February 2002) is a South Korean badminton player, who won the gold medal at the 2024 Summer Olympics in the women's singles event.
She won the gold medals at the 2023 and 2026 World Championships, making history as the first Korean women's singles player to win the World Championships title.
Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri (born 3 January 1976) is a Moroccan politician and lawyer who is the prime minister–designate of Morocco since 29 September 2026. She is the first woman to hold the office.
A member of the Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), she previously served as mayor of Marrakesh, first from 2009 to 2015, and then since 2021.
On 29 September 2026, Mohammed VI received her at the Royal Palace and appointed El Mansouri as Prime Minister of Morocco, becoming the first woman to hold the office.
